name: DJITelloPy
summary: Python wrapper around the official Tello UDP text SDK: takeoff, relative moves, rc sticks, state telemetry and the video stream. Works with Tello, Tello EDU and RoboMaster TT.
why_it_matters: If the hackathon hands out Tellos, this is the fastest path from a planner to a flying drone. All compute stays on the laptop.
hackathon_notes: MIT, pure-Python wheel (djitellopy 2.5.0). Last push 2025-01. No simulator: mock the UDP protocol for dry runs. Tello auto-lands after 15 s without a command, so keep a heartbeat. rc commands have no ack.

name: Olympe
summary: Parrot's Python controller library for ANAFI drones and the Sphinx simulator, using the Arsdk messages (moveBy, moveTo, piloting, camera).
why_it_matters: The SDK path if the event platform is a Parrot ANAFI. Same code drives Sphinx and the real drone.
hackathon_notes: BSD-3-Clause. PyPI ships only a manylinux x86_64 wheel (parrot-olympe 8.5.0), and Sphinx needs Ubuntu x64 plus an NVIDIA GPU, so neither runs on an Apple Silicon Mac. Only useful if an x86 Linux GPU box is provided.

name: MuJoCo Menagerie
summary: Curated MuJoCo MJCF models, including a Skydio X2 quadrotor and a Bitcraze Crazyflie 2. Models only, no controllers.
why_it_matters: Gives a clean quadrotor model in a physics engine that runs natively on Apple Silicon. Useful when you want contacts and rendering without PyBullet.
hackathon_notes: pip install mujoco, clone the repo, load bitcraze_crazyflie_2/scene.xml. You write the controller and the planner loop; budget 1-2 h to first hover. Per-model licenses differ (repo-level NOASSERTION).

name: DJI Mobile SDK V5 (Android) sample
summary: Sample app and docs entry for DJI MSDK V5, the Android SDK for current DJI consumer and enterprise aircraft, including the virtual stick API.
why_it_matters: If the platform is a DJI consumer drone, virtual stick through MSDK is the only way to send setpoints from your own code.
hackathon_notes: Android-only toolchain, DJI app key registration, and aircraft/controller compatibility limits (Mini 4 Pro needs RC-N2 per press). Advanced virtual stick wants 5-25 Hz setpoints. Expect hours before first autonomous move. License NOASSERTION.

name: LSY Autonomous Drone Racing
summary: TUM LSY course project for autonomous Crazyflie racing through gates and around pole obstacles, in simulation (crazyflow) and on real hardware with Vicon. Four TOML difficulty levels add randomized inertia, obstacle and gate positions, and random tracks.
why_it_matters: Closest open analogue to an A=>B-through-obstacles task with a scoring harness. Exact obstacle positions are only revealed within 0.7 m, which forces replanning.
hackathon_notes: MIT, active (push 2026-11). Pure-Python on CPU, so it should run on Apple Silicon (not run here). Copy the level-2 config idea for your own eval: randomize obstacles per episode and report success rate.

name: Crazyflow
summary: JAX-based batched, differentiable quadrotor simulator from TUM LSY with first-principles and identified Crazyflie models, plus MuJoCo/MJX rendering, raycasting and contacts.
why_it_matters: Light, pip-installable Crazyflie sim with sim-to-real tuned dynamics. Runs on CPU, so usable on a Mac.
hackathon_notes: MIT. CPU wheel is py3-none-any; the GPU extra is Linux x86-64 CUDA only. Lower-level than gym-pybullet-drones; use it through lsy_drone_racing unless you need batched rollouts.

name: aerial-autonomy-stack
summary: Dockerized harness to simulate and deploy PX4, ArduPilot and Betaflight drones with ROS 2, YOLO and lidar odometry (KISS-ICP), with a steppable gymnasium interface and Jetson deployment images.
why_it_matters: A worked example of a sim-to-Jetson product pipeline: same containers for sim and the aircraft, offboard interfaces for both autopilots.
hackathon_notes: MIT. Needs an NVIDIA driver and nvidia-container-toolkit; first build about 45 min per README. Not runnable on the Mac. Read it for architecture ideas, do not plan to run it.

name: Genesis World
summary: Python multi-physics simulation platform with camera, depth and lidar sensors and a compiler that targets CUDA, Apple Metal and ARM64. Ships drone hover and route-following examples.
why_it_matters: One of the few GPU-class simulators with a Metal backend, so it can use the Mac GPU for depth and lidar rendering.
hackathon_notes: Apache-2.0, very active. pip install genesis-world. Drone examples in examples/drone/. API changes fast; pin the version on Day 0 and test before relying on it.

name: AirSim Drone Racing Lab
summary: Archived AirSim-based framework used for the NeurIPS 2019 Game of Drones competition: gate tracks, perception, planning and head-to-head racing tiers.
why_it_matters: Shows how a sim competition structured A=>B-through-gates tiers and scoring.
hackathon_notes: MIT, archived 2023. Unreal binaries, not practical on Apple Silicon. Use the paper for format ideas only.

name: agile_autonomy
summary: Code for 'Learning High-Speed Flight in the Wild': a policy trained in simulation from a privileged expert that maps depth and state to collision-free trajectories.
why_it_matters: Reference for learned depth-to-trajectory obstacle flight and its sim-to-real recipe.
hackathon_notes: GPL-3.0, last push 2023-01. Tested on Ubuntu 20.04 + ROS Noetic only, depends on Flightmare. Not buildable on the Mac in 48 h; cite the idea.

name: AI-deck GAP8 examples
summary: Bitcraze examples for the Crazyflie AI-deck GAP8 processor: camera streaming over WiFi and small onboard CNN inference.
why_it_matters: Path to onboard vision on a 30 g drone, which matters if the scoring rewards onboard compute.
hackathon_notes: No license file in the repo. GAP8 toolchain via docker; flashing and model quantisation take hours. Camera streaming to the laptop is the realistic 48 h use.
